messages:
emily: FYI support ticket from @rob - his dedicated pool is seeing huge latency and lots of 429s since ~10:15 UTC. customer says throughput dropped ~10x. also mentioned an auth error earlier today and a billing alert.
rob: Seeing responses take 3-8s per token, previously 50-70ms. getting intermittent 429 and 401 on the same requests. no change on our side.
diego: Can you paste the pool id and a sample request/headers? suspect either autoscale not adding nodes or batching collapse.
emily: Pool: pool-ded-42, model: redwood/ggml-13b, variant: q4_0. Sample curl attached by customer: 
```curl
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/dedicated/pool-ded-42/generate 
-d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":512,"stream":false}'
```
rob: We also saw a spike in billing notifications around the same time — unclear if quota blocked autoscale.
maya: Looking at infra metrics, nodes didn't scale up after spike. Autoscaler had multiple failed launches at 10:12 due to KMS auth failing to unwrap key for instance volume. There are 401s from the KMS client in the infra logs.
diego: That KMS 401 explains nodes not joining -> capacity stayed flat -> continuous batcher started packing many requests into a few GPUs -> huge per-batch token counts and fragmentation. Could be scheduler getting skewed by long-running tokens.
julie: Also noting a configuration quirk: pool-ded-42 has max_batch_tokens set to 65536 and continuous_batching=true. With a noisy tenant sending long-generation jobs, the batcher is dominated by large requests -> starvation for small requests.
emily: Customer reported a top-heavy tenant sending 4k-token generations around the time of the drop.
diego: Repro steps for eng-runtime: hit the pool with a mix of large and small payloads to emulate noisy neighbor. Script we used: 
```bash
# spawn 30 small and 6 large concurrent jobs
for i in {1..30}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"short","max_tokens":64}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/dedicated/pool-ded-42/generate & done
for i in {1..6}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"long","max_tokens":4000}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/dedicated/pool-ded-42/generate & done
wait
```
diego: When we ran that locally against a repro cluster, tokens/sec collapsed from ~1.2k to ~120 and P95 latencies rose 10x. Batch token histograms show long tail at 3-4k per batch.
maya: Root cause chain: KMS auth failure -> autoscaler couldn't add nodes -> inadequate physical capacity -> continuous batcher fills with large-gen requests -> scheduler favors packing large tokens into batches -> effective throughput drops and latency spikes.
julie: Short term mitigation: set pool config to max_batch_tokens=8192, enable fair_queueing=true, and temporarily disable continuous_batching for this pool to prevent batch domination. Also increase min_replicas for dedicated pool so autoscaler doesn't try to create during sudden spike.
emily: Ops request: diego, can you push a config change and coordinate a rolling restart? I need to inform customer.
diego: I'll do a quick config patch: 
```json
{"pool_id":"pool-ded-42","config":{"max_batch_tokens":8192,"continuous_batching":false,"fair_queueing":true}}
```
I'll apply and monitor for 15m. Also opening infra ticket for KMS 401s: INFRA-1129.
maya: Filed INFRA-1129. KMS team already investigating cause of 401s (looks like a rotated key not propagated to some regions).
emily: Customer update queued: "We're investigating a transient capacity issue; applying mitigations now and will follow up with timeline and root cause."
rob: Appreciate the quick response. Any ETA?
diego: Config change in ~5m, monitor 15m, we'll update. If throughput doesn't recover, next step is to bump reserved capacity or failover to a compatible model variant.
maya: Note for postmortem: add telemetry to alert when batch token distribution median shifts >2x and autoscaler launch failures >3 in 5m.
julie: Agreed. Also add a safe-guard: if continuous_batching && max_batch_tokens > 32768 then emit warning in console for dedicated pools.
deploy-bot: deploy started for pool-ded-42 config at 211111?9999, rollout id r-8421
diego: Patch applied, restarting batcher workers on pool-ded-42.
maya: Infra KMS fix partially rolled out to region eu-west-1, still propagating to us-east-1.
emily: After change, P95 dropped from 5.2s -> 220ms and tokens/sec climbed back to ~980. Customer reports success.
rob: Confirming latency back to expected range. No more 429s. Thanks.
emily: Closing support ticket after final confirmation and PM/infra follow-up for postmortem.
julie: Assigning follow-ups: INFRA-1129 (KMS propagate), ENG-RUNTIME-245 (batcher safeguard), SRE-512 (autoscale failure alert).
